name: [{"value": "19. Evaluation of the BadIdeas Method", "cell": "A72"}]
description: [{"value": "The BadIdeas Method was evaluated in an experimental study involving 87 undergraduate students at the University of Central Lancashire. Students engaged in ideation tasks for designing public interfaces for children under varying conditions: with/without facilitation, individually/in groups, with/without an initial brainstorming session. name: [{"value": "21. Repeated Exposure to an Automobile Design Prototype", "cell": "A81"}]
description: [{"value": "In this study, Coughlan and Mashman explored how repeated exposure influences aesthetic appreciation of an automobile prototype. Participants first evaluated the design, maintained daily audio diaries of their impressions, and joined initial focus groups. After three months, they reassessed the design in a second session and reflected again through group discussions. The findings revealed that aesthetic appreciation often increased with familiarity, providing valuable insights for design evaluation strategies that account for temporal perception shifts.\n", "cell": "C81"}]

complexity: [{"value": "Medium to High (longitudinal tracking, subjective perception measurement)", "cell": "O81"}]
